primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Plaque psoriasis driven by the IL-23/IL-17 axis
mechanism: Activated dendritic cells and other innate immune cells produce IL-23, which sustains IL-17-producing T-cell populations. IL-17A and related cytokines act on keratinocytes to drive hyperproliferation, impaired differentiation, chemokine and antimicrobial-peptide production, and neutrophil recruitment, creating a self-amplifying inflammatory circuit.
vignette: A 33-year-old man has a chronic relapsing eruption of sharply demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale on the elbows, knees, and scalp. Skin biopsy shows regular epidermal hyperplasia with parakeratosis, diminished granular layer, dilated papillary dermal capillaries, and neutrophils within the stratum corneum.
lead: Which cytokine interaction most directly sustains the epidermal hyperplasia and neutrophilic inflammation in this disorder?
correct: IL-23–dependent maintenance of IL-17-producing lymphocytes, with IL-17 acting on keratinocytes to amplify inflammation and proliferation
distractors: IL-4–dependent differentiation of Th2 cells, with IL-13 suppressing epidermal barrier proteins
IFN-gamma activation of macrophages, causing caseating granuloma formation within the dermis
IL-5–mediated eosinophil maturation followed by IgE-dependent mast-cell degranulation
TGF-beta–driven fibroblast activation causing progressive replacement of epidermis by dense collagen
distractor_notes: Th2/IL-4/IL-13 signaling is central to atopic dermatitis biology, not the dominant IL-23/IL-17 inflammatory circuit of plaque psoriasis.

IFN-gamma–activated macrophages participate in granulomatous inflammation, but psoriasis is characterized by keratinocyte hyperproliferation and T17/neutrophilic inflammation rather than caseating dermal granulomas.
IL-5/eosinophil and IgE/mast-cell pathways are typical of type I allergic/eosinophilic responses and do not explain the psoriatic histology.
TGF-beta can promote fibrosis, but plaque psoriasis is not a fibrosing replacement disorder; its epidermal thickening reflects accelerated keratinocyte proliferation and abnormal differentiation.
key_expl: This is plaque psoriasis. A central pathogenic circuit is the IL-23/IL-17 axis. IL-23 supports expansion and maintenance of IL-17-producing lymphocytes; IL-17A then acts strongly on keratinocytes, inducing proliferation, abnormal differentiation, antimicrobial peptides, cytokines, and chemokines that recruit additional inflammatory cells, including neutrophils. This feed-forward loop explains acanthosis, parakeratosis, and neutrophilic aggregates such as Munro microabscesses. The importance of this pathway is also reflected by the effectiveness of IL-17- and IL-23-targeted therapies.
objective: Explain plaque psoriasis as an IL-23/IL-17-driven inflammatory circuit in which IL-17-responsive keratinocytes proliferate and recruit additional immune cells, including neutrophils.
clues: well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale
